html:
The Kawaiisu are a small Native American people of the Tehachapi Mountains and the nearby Mojave Desert edge in southern California. The map spells their name Kawahsu.

They speak a Southern Numic language of the Uto-Aztecan family, close to that of the Southern Paiute. They gathered acorns and pinyon nuts, hunted, and moved between mountain and desert with the seasons. Their neighbours were the Yokuts to the west and the Serrano to the south.

Little is written about them before the 1800s. Settlers, ranchers and the railway took their land, and their language now has very few speakers. The map also shows them under the name Kawaiisu.
sum: The Kawaiisu are a small Native American people of the Tehachapi Mountains and the nearby Mojave Desert edge in southern California. The map spells their name Kawahsu.
